title: Chebyshev Type I Filter (CHEBY1)
summary: A second order Chebyshev Type I lowpass that trades a controlled bump near the cutoff period for a steeper cut of faster price swings.
descriptionHtml:
The Chebyshev Type I Filter is a recursive second order lowpass. Compared with a maximally flat design it allows a ripple in the passband, and in return its response falls away more steeply past the cutoff.

The cutoff is wc = 2 pi / length, pre-warped with tan(wc / 2). The ripple in decibels sets epsilon = sqrt(10 ^ (ripple / 10) - 1), and from it the analogue pole is placed using the hyperbolic sine and cosine of half of asinh(1 / epsilon). The pole is mapped to a digital biquad with the bilinear transform, and each bar's output combines the current and two previous prices with the two previous outputs. The coefficients add up so that a flat price passes unchanged. The first two bars are seeded with the price, and a missing price borrows the previous one.

In this design the ripple shows up as a single bump: swings with a period equal to the length are passed at 10 ^ (ripple / 20) times their size (about 12 percent larger at the default 1 dB), and below that period the response drops quickly. At the defaults, half of a swing's power is gone at a period of about 11 bars.
howToReadHtml:
Use it as a smoothing line. Price above a rising line points to an upward short-term direction, and below a falling line to a downward one. Turns in the line mark changes in the smoothed direction.

The ripple setting changes both the shape and the reach of the filter. A larger ripple enlarges swings near the length period and makes the line overshoot after a sudden jump (by about 15 percent of the jump at 1 dB, and more at higher values). A very small ripple removes the bump but moves the cutoff to much shorter periods, so the line smooths far less: at 0.01 dB and the default length of 20 it passes most swings down to about 6 bars.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series the filter smooths. The close by default.

settings.label: Length
settings.html: The cutoff period in bars. Swings at this period are passed with the ripple bump; much shorter swings are cut.

settings.label: Passband Ripple (dB)
settings.html: The size of the bump near the cutoff, in decibels. More ripple gives a steeper cut and more overshoot; less ripple gives a flatter but much weaker filter.

faq.q: What does the ripple setting change?
faq.html: It sets how much swings near the length period are enlarged, 10 ^ (ripple / 20) times at that period. A larger ripple buys a steeper drop for faster swings; a smaller one flattens the response but shifts the cutoff toward much shorter periods.

faq.q: Why can the line overshoot after a sharp move?
faq.html: The bump in the response comes with ringing. After a sudden jump the line goes past the new level before settling: about 15 percent of the jump at 1 dB, and more as the ripple grows.
No. The first two bars are seeded with the price, so the line starts on the first bar and settles over the next few lengths.

related.title: Chebyshev Type II Filter (CHEBY2)
related.summary: A second order recursive lowpass with zeros placed among fast swings, rescaled so a flat price passes unchanged; the attenuation setting shapes how it treats the fastest noise.

related.title: Christiano-Fitzgerald Band-Pass Filter (CFITZ)
related.summary: An asymmetric band-pass filter on the close that weights past bars so the weights sum to zero, giving a cycle line that swings around zero.

related.title: EDCF: Ehlers Distance Coefficient Filter
related.summary: A weighted average whose weights are each bar's summed squared distance from the bars before it, so it turns quickly on sharp moves.
